questions.prompt: How many pillars does the AWS Well-Architected Framework have?
questions.explanation: There are six pillars. Sustainability was added in 2021, bringing the count from five to six.

questions.prompt: Which of these are pillars of the Well-Architected Framework? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Security, Reliability, and Sustainability are three of the six pillars (with Operational Excellence, Performance Efficiency, and Cost Optimization). Marketing is not a pillar.

questions.prompt: Which pillar was added most recently, and is often forgotten?
questions.explanation: Sustainability was added in 2021, taking the framework from five to six pillars, and is the one people most often overlook.

options.text: No — it means making deliberate trade-offs between pillars aligned to business priorities

questions.explanation: The pillars can pull against each other (e.g., reliability vs cost). Being well-architected means choosing deliberate trade-offs that fit business priorities, not maxing one.

questions.prompt: Match each pillar to a representative concern.

pairs.right: Recovering from failure and scaling correctly

questions.explanation: Each pillar has a focus: operations/improvement, protecting assets, correct and resilient operation, and getting the most value per dollar.

questions.prompt: A general design principle of the framework is to stop guessing ____ and instead scale with demand.
questions.explanation: "Stop guessing capacity" is a core design principle — scale elastically with demand rather than over-provisioning fixed capacity.
